messages:
Sam (Support): Hey team — Maya's integration started failing when they switch active project IDs. They get a 403 with 'org/project mismatch'. Customer gave this request id: req_0abc1234 and says it used to work earlier today.

Maya (Customer): repro steps: 1) auth with service key for org `acme-org` 2) call /v1/generate with header `X-Project-ID: proj-42` -> 403. We tried swapping project header to proj-7 and it worked.

Sam (Support): Paste of curl they ran:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \n  -H "X-Org-ID: acme-org" \n  -H "X-Project-ID: proj-42" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Sam (Support): Response snippet they got: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`
{"error":"org/project mismatch","request_id":"req_0abc1234"}

Nina (Eng): thanks — couple quick asks: can you share the raw response headers (we want X-Request-Id from gateway and any X-Auth-Info headers). Also confirm whether the token is an org-scoped key or project-scoped. Project-scoped tokens will 403 if project != token.project.

Maya (Customer): headers from the failing call (redacted):
`X-Request-Id: req_0abc1234`
`X-Gateway: gw-3`
`X-Auth-Info: scope=org:acme-org`

Alex (eng-oncall): quick hypothesis: token is org-scoped but the project header is for a project outside that org or vice versa. Can you run a curl that hits /v1/auth/inspect (internal endpoint) to decode token? Example we asked customers to run:
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/inspect | jq .
```
It will show `org_id`, `project_id` embedded in token.

Maya (Customer): ran inspect, got `{"org_id":"acme-org","project_id":null,"scopes":["org:acme-org"]}`

Nina (Eng): ok that confirms token is org-scoped (no project bound). Org-scoped keys should allow any project in the same org, so weird that proj-42 is failing. Two things to gather: the gateway logs around req_0abc1234 and the auth service log for token validation. If you can upload a debug bundle to our collector that includes the raw request headers + client IP + timestamp (we need 2024-06-04T14:32:10Z-ish) that'll speed root cause.

Sam (Support): sending upload link to Maya via DM :lock: (internal only). Maya, include the full -v curl output (headers + TLS peer info) and timestamp.

Maya (Customer): uploaded bundle (link: internal). Also one more datapoint: when they removed `X-Org-ID` header entirely and only sent Authorization + X-Project-ID: proj-42 it succeeded. So including X-Org-ID seems to trigger the 403.

Alex (eng-oncall): aha. That suggests our gateway is preferring explicit X-Org-ID over token-derived org and maybe validating cross-check incorrectly. Could be a regression in the header precedence logic (we recently changed header order in routing).

Nina (Eng): can eng team reproduce locally? Steps I will try: use an org-scoped token + set X-Org-ID to a different org than the token -> expect 403. set X-Org-ID to same org -> should pass. Also test case where X-Project-ID belongs to the token org.

Alex (eng-oncall): reproducer command (my sandbox):
```bash
# token belongs to acme-org
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_acme" -H "X-Org-ID: other-org" -H "X-Project-ID: proj-42" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Expected: 403 with `org/project mismatch`. If we get that locally, it's a bug.

Sam (Support): Nina, can you ask auth/gateway owners to grep for req_0abc1234 in prod logs? I noted the gateway sent `X-Auth-Validated: true` but then returned 403.

Nina (Eng): already on it, pinged @gateway-team and @auth-team, attaching query we ran:
```sql
select * from gateway_logs where request_id='req_0abc1234' limit 20;
```
Found records: auth_check passed, routed to model-service, model-service returned 403 with message 'explicit-org-header mismatches token org'

Alex (eng-oncall): that message lines up with a new validation we shipped last week that enforces header-token consistency. Looks like a legit enforcement path but it's overly strict when X-Org-ID is present but empty or canonicalized differently (case/whitespace).

Maya (Customer): helpful to know. Is there a short-term workaround?

Sam (Support): temporary workaround: omit the `X-Org-ID` header (as you found) or ensure it exactly matches token org id (case-sensitive). We'll keep you posted.

Nina (Eng): action items: 1) eng to add a tolerant canonicalization (trim + lower) and allow token-derived org to win when header is empty/whitespace. 2) add clearer error text with `expected_org`/`token_org` in response so support can triage faster. 3) backport hotfix to gateway if regression confirmed.

support-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident created: INC-2024-2247 — label `auth-gateway-org-header` assigned.

Sam (Support): thanks team. Maya — we'll follow up once we have a patch, ETA for hotfix is ~2-4 hours. Please keep the debug bundle available if we need more traces. :pray:

Maya (Customer): thanks all :thumbsup:

Alex (eng-oncall): closing loop — reproduced locally, prepping patch. will post PR and link to staging diff here.

Nina (Eng): PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/+/2345 (staging) — includes canonicalization + improved error payload. Rolling to staging now.

Sam (Support): great. I'll update the customer thread with workaround and expected ETA.

support-bot: Note: remember to sanitize uploads. Do not include full secrets in debug bundles.
